steps: Check site & approvals

Confirm the stove and connector meet all clearances and the floor protection is adequate; get approvals from the local building officials. The data plate on the back of the stove lists the testing lab and installation requirements.
Prepare the fireplace
Minimum masonry fireplace: height (A) 21¼", depth (B) 19¼", width (C) 28¾". Remove or lock the damper open and permanently seal any gap between the fireplace and facing masonry.

Height (A)21¼" / 540 mm
Depth (B)19¼" / 490 mm
Width (C)28¾" / 730 mm
  • The chimney must have a clay liner or a stainless steel liner.
  • Remove or lock existing fireplace dampers in the open position.
  • Permanently seal any opening between the masonry of the fireplace and the facing masonry.
  • Use the steel box as a template; allow extra room, especially above the insert.
Note: p. 5 says do not move bricks or mortar from the existing fireplace; p. 4 describes making adjustments to the masonry surrounding the insert, and p. 8 calls for a metal data tag where a masonry fireplace has been altered to accommodate the insert.
Unpack & remove the door
Ships fully assembled at 327 lbs: use two people and an underlay. Pull the split pin on each hinge pin, lift out both pins and the door; keep the loose brass washer from the upper hinge.
Remove liners & insulation
Bottom liners, both side liners, the rear liner, then the liner and insulation mat above the baffle plate. The liners are very porous: handle with great care.
Remove the baffle plate
30 lbs on four M8 bolts. Remove the outermost bolt each side, thread in the two headless guide bolts, remove the two center bolts, then slide the baffle off the guides.
Connect the flue collar
Unscrew the flue collar with its stop bar and connect it to the flue pipe (or 8 feet stainless steel connector) or the flexible chimney liner inside the fireplace opening.
Level & mount
Level the convection box in the opening (Allen-head bolts under the base liners) and mount the combustion chamber. Pass the collar and liner through the rear hole and fasten the collar back on.
Reassemble the firebox
Refit the baffle, liners, insulation mat and front liner in reverse order, and rehang the door. If the masonry was altered, attach the enclosed metal data tag where it is easily visible.

1. Baffle plate back over the two guide bolts; screw in the two M8 center bolts; remove the guide bolts; insert and screw in the last two M8 bolts.
  2. Liners back in this order: the rear liner, the two side liners, the two bottom liners.
  3. Insulation mat carefully on top of the baffle plate, then the last liner in front, centered on the baffle plate and slanted up towards the smoke exit hole.
  4. Door back on its hinges with the hinge pins; split pins and the brass washer back on the upper hinge.

Where a masonry fireplace has been altered to accommodate the insert, attach the enclosed metal data tag to the masonry fireplace with screws or nails, easily visible to future homeowners. To remove the insert later for inspection, follow the installation (page 6-8) in reverse order.
Secure the connector
6 inches (150mm) connector: 24 MSG black or blue, or listed double wall; never galvanized. Minimum of three screws to the product and each adjoining section; flue system independently secured.
Clearances, hearth & air
Verify clearances A–E, floor protection for the door-glass height, 42 inches to furniture, and a fresh air inlet where needed. Do not install in a mobile home.

Sidewall to insert (A)17" · 432 mm
Combustible mantel to insert (B)28½" · 724 mm
Side facing (C)8" · 200 mm
Top facing (E)28½" · 724 mm

Hearth extension (D) depends on the height from the floor to the bottom of the door glass: 6" or more needs R-value 1.79 protection 21" in front and 8" to each side of the loading door; 20.25" or more needs non-combustible ember protection 16" in front and 8" to each side (US figures).

Furniture: recommended minimum 42 inches. Fresh air inlet: 2 square inches (1250 square mm) of free air space. If acid-washing the masonry, protect the stove with an acid-proof cover. Do not install in a mobile home.

panels.title: Smoke or sluggish fire
items: Smoke or fumes on lighting or reloading, or the fire won't respond → poor draft; upgrade the flue system
In a very few cases → not enough fresh air getting into the room
Stove suddenly sluggish → soot fall around the flue collar or in the flue/chimney
Overly dry, gray wood → back-puffing and sluggishness
Flue significantly larger than 6" → flue gases cool, sluggish or unpredictable performance

panels.title: Over-firing & fast wear
items: Any part of the stove or chimney connector glows → overfiring
Baffle distorted by an overfire → still works, efficiency may suffer; replace it
Persistent heavy firing, or soot and ashes left to accumulate → fast internal wear

panels.title: Dirty glass
items: Fuel too wet, or wood not well seasoned
Logs too large or not split
Combustion temperatures too low, or the stove run too slowly
Wood spits or sizzles and the glass mists up → wood not properly seasoned

panels.title: Won't catch or hard to control
items: New wood won't light → leave the door slightly ajar until it kindles
Logs not alight within 2 minutes → in an extreme case the flue gases may ignite; reload onto a good ember layer
Rope gasket hardened, air leaking around the door → fire less controllable; fit a Morsø rope gasket kit

fire.title: Lighting a fire
fire.html:
Morsø recommends the top-down method. It's the most environmentally friendly way to light, and it minimizes soot on the glass.

  1. Open the air fully: slide the air control lever under the door all the way to the right.
  2. Lay about 4-6 lbs of dry kindling sticks, a layer 5-6 inches thick. Put two firelighters directly under the top layer of kindling.
  3. Light the fire.
  4. Leave the door open an inch or two so plenty of air gets in. Don't leave the stove while the door is open.
  5. After about 5 minutes, when the chimney is warm, close the door. A good layer of embers forms after about 15-20 minutes. Then add wood (see Reload the fire).
Your first fire: keep it small, so the paint can cure and the stove's main plates can settle into position. The paint gives off some fumes, so ventilate the room.
Note: p. 15 calls for 4-6 lbs of kindling; the safety summary on p. 28 says to use 1 - 2 kg of kindling.
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
You run the fire with one lever: the air control beneath the door. It slides sideways and sets the primary air.

All the way leftMinimum low burn rate (set by Morsø)
Mid rangeMedium burn rate (recommended)
All the way rightHigh burn rate, air fully open
  • Open it fully to light the fire and when you reload.
  • Before you go to the low burn rate, burn at medium for about 15 minutes so the fire is properly established.
  • When you turn the air down, keep enough for clear, lasting flames. Clear, yellow flames mean enough air.
  • Less heat: less wood, less air. More heat: more wood, more air. Keep a good layer of embers either way.
  • Burning too slowly puts soot on the glass and creosote in the chimney.

Primary air also washes down the back of the glass. Two other air supplies can't be adjusted: secondary air burns off leftover gases at the top of the fire, and pilot air feeds the embers from behind the front grate.

Don't try to get more heat by changing the air control's range. The minimum low burn rate is set by the manufacturer, and altering it is against federal regulations.

reload.title: Reloading the fire
reload.html:
Add wood while there are still glowing embers in the bed.

  1. Spread the embers across the bottom, with most of them toward the front.
  2. Lay 2-3 pieces of wood across the embers, in one or two layers, about 1 inch apart.
  3. Close the door and leave the air fully open. If the wood doesn't catch, leave the door slightly ajar until it does, then close it.
  4. After a few minutes, set the air control for the heat you want.

The new wood should light within 2 minutes. If the logs don't ignite, in an extreme case the flue gases can ignite and cause damage or injury. Always reload onto a good layer of embers.

  • Keep the wood below the back stone and the stainless-steel air baffle box.
  • Keep logs at least one inch from the glass.
  • Don't prop the wood up on grates or andirons.
Note: p. 16 recommends a load of 4 lbs (3 pieces) up to 12 lbs (6 pieces); p. 17 recommends 4 lbs (2 pieces) up to 12 lbs (6 pieces), with a maximum of 6 kg/12 lbs per load (approx 5-6 split logs). The safety summary on p. 28 says to refuel with 2 - 3 pieces, no more than 2 - 2.5 kg.

wood.title: Choosing your wood
wood.html:
Any natural wood can be burned, as long as it's well seasoned and dry.

Lengthapprox. 10-11 inches (27 cm)
Thicknessapprox. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm), split
Weight per piecearound 1.5-2 lbs
Moistureno more than 20%
Maker's website: Log Size 20".

Split the wood so it dries. Stack it under cover where air moves through every piece. Soft woods can season in one good summer; oak, maple and elm may need up to 18 months. Seasoned wood feels light and shows cracks running out from the center at the ends. A Morsø Moisture Meter (part # 62929900) checks the moisture.

If your wood spits or sizzles and the glass keeps misting up, it isn't seasoned enough. Very dry, gray wood can cause back-puffing and a sluggish fire.

Never burn unseasoned or treated wood, driftwood (its salt can cause corrosion), construction wood, colored paper, cardboard, solvents, trash or garbage.
Note: p. 14 gives a split thickness of approx. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm); the safety summary on p. 28 says 8 - 12 cm thick.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
When the stove runs at the right temperature, the glass stays mostly clean. Dirt that settles while you light usually burns off as the fire gets hotter.

For deposits that won't burn off

  • Wait until the glass is cold. Never clean it while it's hot.
  • Use Morsø glass cleaner, following its instructions.
  • Never use abrasive cleaners on the glass.

Why the glass gets dirty

  • The wood is too wet or not well seasoned.
  • The logs are too large or not split.
  • The fire burns too cool, or the stove is run too slowly.
Cracked or broken glass: don't use the stove until it's replaced. Use only Morsø high temperature ceramic glass (part # 79560100) from your Morsø dealer. To avoid breaking it, don't strike the glass or slam the door.

Old ceramic glass can't go in ordinary glass recycling. Hand it in at a recycling station as ceramic glass.

ash.title: Removing ash
ash.html:
Don't take out all the ash. Always keep a 1-1.5 inch (2-3 cm) layer of ash on the floor of the firebox.

Removing ash safely

  • Never empty the stove while it's burning.
  • Never use a household or shop vacuum to remove ash.
  • Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid.
  • Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn.
  • If you bury the ashes or spread them outside, keep them in the closed container until all the cinders have cooled completely.
Ash left in a stove you aren't using soaks up moisture and leads to rust. Clean the stove out thoroughly when the heating season ends.

chimney.title: Chimney care & creosote
chimney.html:
Burning wood slowly makes tar and vapors that condense in the cool chimney as creosote. If creosote ignites, it makes an extremely hot fire, so remove it when it builds up.

How often

  • At first, check for soot above the baffle plate and around the flue outlet every month or so.
  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months during the heating season.
  • Clean the flue after each heating season, and inspect it before the next one for bird's nests or other blockages.

To look yourself, let the stove cool completely, then use a mirror to sight up through the flue collar into the chimney. If you can't inspect or clean it yourself, call a professional chimney sweep or your Morsø dealer.

A stove that suddenly turns sluggish may have soot fallen around the flue collar or in the chimney. Smoke coming out when you light or reload is almost certainly poor draft; ask your stove supplier about improving the flue.

If you have a chimney fire

  1. Close the air control.
  2. Get everyone out of the house.
  3. Call the Fire Department.

safety.title: Safety & over-firing
safety.html:
• Don't over-fire. If any part of the stove or the chimney connector glows, you are over-firing. That can cause a house fire or permanently damage the stove.
  • Run it with the door fully closed to reduce the risk of smoke and flame spilling out. Never leave the stove unattended with the door open: gas and flame can be drawn out of the opening.
  • It gets hot. Keep children, clothing and furniture away. Touching it can burn skin.
  • Keep furniture at least 42 inches from the stove, and the same for drying clothes, newspapers, firewood and other things that can burn.
  • Never let the fire rest against the glass.
  • Burn only solid wood. The wrong fuel can give off toxic fumes.
  • Never burn overnight.
Morsø recommends a smoke detector in the room where the stove is installed.
Don't use the stove if the door glass is damaged. Replace broken glass right away.

service.title: Yearly care & summer storage
service.html:
Before each heating season, clean, inspect and repair:

  • Clean the chimney and chimney connector thoroughly.
  • Inspect the chimney for damage. Weak sections of a prefabricated chimney get replaced; a mason repairs a masonry chimney.
  • Replace any damaged sections of the chimney connector.
  • Check the gaskets for wear or compression.
  • Check the glass for cracks.
  • Check the door and handles for tightness.

Door gasket

The rope gasket around the door can harden over time. Replace it if the door gets hard to close, or if air leaks in around the door and the fire gets harder to control. Your stove supplier has a Morsø rope gasket kit.

Leaving it unused

Clean the stove out thoroughly and leave the air control slightly open so air keeps moving through it. A desiccant such as kitty litter in the bottom absorbs moisture over the summer; remove it before the heating season. Use a chimney cap to keep rain out, but don't block the flue completely.

Wear safety goggles and gloves for maintenance, and always use original Morsø spare parts.

warranty.title: Morsø guarantee
warranty.html:
Morsø offers a 10-Year Manufacturers Guarantee against manufacturing defects in the main exterior body parts of the stove. It applies when the stove was supplied by an authorized Morsø dealer.

Not covered

  • The flame-path parts: firebricks, glass, baffle, pilot air assembly and flue collar
  • The ceramic rope
  • The paint finish

Flame-path parts take the full heat of the fire and need replacing from time to time as routine maintenance. Get them from your Morsø dealer and don't use substitutes. Replace damaged parts as soon as possible to avoid further damage.

The guarantee page points you online to read more about the guarantee and to register your new stove.

specFlue.title: Chimney, liner & connector
specFlue.html:
Chimney linercontinuous, 6" diameter, insert to top of chimney
Connector and chimney insidenot less than 6 inches diameter (or equivalent cross section)
Connector6 inches (150mm) diameter
Stainless steel connectorat least 8 feet
Chimney height16 feet, flue collar to top
Maker's website: Flue outlet top 150; Flue outlet rear 150. Install to the manual.
  • Residential masonry chimney, or listed type HT factory-built: UL-103-1985 (2100º F.) USA, ULC S-629 (650ºC) Canada. Factory-built: connector, insulated High Temperature flueliner (16 feet), High Temperature chimney cap.
  • Liner system UL listed to UL 1777 (USA) / ULC S635 (Canada); class 3 of CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640.
  • One flueway per appliance: never a flue serving another appliance, never an air distribution duct or system.
  • Flue system independently secured; it must not rely on the stove for support.
  • Flue collar takes the enclosed 6 inch adapter. Connector: 24 MSG black or blue, or listed double wall for solid fuel; single wall 24 gauge or heavier; no galvanized.
  • Minimum of three screws to the product and each adjoining section. Mild bends (45º vs. 90º); all parts accessible for cleaning; not through an attic, closet or concealed space.
  • Not significantly larger than 6": flue gases cool excessively and the stove turns sluggish or unpredictable.
Note: p. 9 says the insert must be installed with a continuous 6" liner from the insert to the top of the chimney; p. 5 says the chimney must have a clay liner or a stainless steel liner, with a stainless steel connector at least 8 feet long; and p. 7 offers the 8 feet stainless steel connector as an alternative to the flexible chimney liner.
Note: p. 9 recommends a chimney height of at least 16 feet (not required); the sample installation on p. 11 labels the flueliner "Minimum 16' high".

specWeight.title: Weight & handling
specWeight.html:
Insert327 lbs
Baffle plate30 lbs
Maker's website: Gross Weight 275 lbs.

Ships fully assembled. Two people are recommended for unpacking and installing; lay parts on an underlay (cardboard, rug or the like). The liner is connected from inside the insert, so the door, liners, insulation and baffle come out first. Install so the insert can later be removed without damaging the masonry or other materials around it.

specFreshAir.title: Fresh air inlet
specFreshAir.html:
Free air space2 square inches (1250 square mm)

As printed: "Unless there is deemed to be insufficient residual air into the room via doorways, windows and the like, a dedicated fresh air inlet will be needed." It is particularly important in a well-sealed room, or where an extractor hood or ventilation system disturbs the natural air pressure.

  • Not on a wall usually subject to negative pressure from normal wind patterns.
  • Not directly across the room from the stove (cold air draft).
  • Air flow within the insert may not be altered.
The sentence above reads as a double negative; the local building officials have the final authorization on the installation.

conflicts.issue: Approved fireplace types: p. 5 says the installation may be used with a factory built or masonry fireplace; p. 12 lists only a masonry fireplace or the Morsø Fireplace Insert Zero Clearance Enclosure as approved in the US and Canada.

Masonry alteration: p. 5 says do not move bricks or mortar from the existing fireplace; p. 4 describes adjustments to the masonry surrounding the insert (steel box as template) and p. 8 calls for a metal data tag where a masonry fireplace has been altered to accommodate the insert.

Liner requirement: p. 9 says the insert must be installed with a continuous 6'' chimney liner from the insert to the top of the chimney; p. 5 says the chimney must have a clay liner or a stainless steel liner and the stainless steel connector must be at least 8 feet long; p. 7 offers the 8 feet stainless steel connector as an alternative to the flexible chimney liner.
Chimney height: p. 9 recommends at least 16 feet (not required); the p. 11 sample installation labels the flueliner 'Minimum 16' high'.

Load size: p. 16 recommends 4 lbs (3 pieces) up to 12 lbs (6 pieces); p. 17 says 4 lbs (2 pieces) up to 12 lbs (6 pieces) and a maximum of 6 kg/12 lbs per load (approx 5-6 split logs); the p. 28 safety summary says refuel with 2 - 3 pieces, no more than 2 - 2.5 kg.
Kindling amount: p. 15 says 4-6 lbs (5-6 inches thickness) of dry kindling; the p. 28 safety summary says 1 - 2 kg.
Split size: p. 14 says approx. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm) in section; the p. 28 safety summary says 8 - 12 cm thick.

review.notes: One 28-page 2021 North America installation & operation manual (72561400); printed page numbers match physical pages. Pages 25-26 are blank; the p. 22 parts diagram is position numbers only (Danish revision notes) and was not used; the p. 23-24 parts list was used only to confirm the glass part number. No troubleshooting chart or code table: fault panels come from the manual's draft, over-firing, wear, dirty-glass and gasket text (pp. 9, 14, 16-20, 28); codes left empty. The p. 28 'How to heat safely' sheet is metric and differs from the operating pages on kindling, split size and refuel load: flagged as three conflicts, not resolved. The p. 13 fresh-air sentence reads as a double negative ('Unless there is deemed to be insufficient residual air ... a dedicated fresh air inlet will be needed'); quoted as printed. The manual describes only a room fresh-air inlet, no outside-air kit (catalog says outside air 'available'). The manual gives no firebox volume, heating area, unit dimensions or maximum log length, so those catalog values could not be checked; it also does not state floor protection when the door glass is less than 6" above a combustible floor. Fireplace letters A-C and clearance letters A-E come from the text tables; the drawings showing where they are measured were not transcribed. Comma decimals printed as 1,5-2 lbs and 1-1,5 inch are shown as 1.5; fractions printed as 211⁄4”, 191⁄4”, 283⁄4” are shown as 21¼", 19¼", 28¾". 'spilt pin' written as split pin; '24 MSG' kept as printed. Catalog model number 64566721 does not appear in the manual. The guarantee page (p. 27) sends owners online for full terms and registration; only the printed terms are summarized.
